summary: Multiplexed gRPC streams + batch GraphQL causing apparent tenant-vs-route accounting skew and intermittent 429s
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports intermittent 429 responses from our hosted API while concurrently running long-lived gRPC multiplexed streams (low-latency chat) and periodic GraphQL batch ingestion jobs against the same tenant API key. Console shows tenant token bucket refilling, but routes are seeing sporadic throttles.

Observed start: 2026-03-09 22:00 UTC. Customer first reported via #support with sample traces attached.

Impact:
- Customer-facing production jobs experiencing ~1-3% 429s on chat low-latency paths during their hourly batch ingest pulse.
- Time-sensitive SLAs for low-latency inference impacted; retries cause higher P99 latency.

Expected behavior:
- Tenant-level quota and per-route windows should be isolated such that a bursty batch ingestion does not cause persistent 429s on multiplexed streaming chat routes for the same tenant key when per-route isolation is enabled.

Attachments: request/response captures, nakeds logs excerpt in reproduction_logs field, screenshots of Console quota graphs.
impact: Production traffic for Acme Analytics chat endpoints receiving intermittent 429s correlated with hourly batch ingestion spikes. Customer reports degradation of near-real-time dashboards and increased retry traffic.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use a single tenant API key with two workloads: A) 100 concurrent gRPC multiplexed streams that hold connections open (chat-like traffic), B) every hour launch a GraphQL batch job that sends 2k embedding calls over parallel HTTP/1.1 requests.
2) Observe Console: tenant token window shows refill immediately after bucket drain; route-specific metrics show transient 429 spikes on the streaming route for ~30-90s following the batch pulse.
3) Collect traces at edge and rate-limiter for 429 responses including Token headers.
reproduction_logs: [2026-03-09T22:01:10.123Z] edge-01 INFO request_id=abc123 api_key=acct:acme path=/v1/stream chat_session open: concurrent_streams=98
[2026-03-09T22:01:13.451Z] rate-limiter WARN token_window_depleted tenant=acct:acme route=/v1/stream remaining=0 refill_in=12s
[2026-03-09T22:01:20.999Z] billing-meter INFO batch_ingest job=embed-pulse size=2048 parallel=32 tenant=acct:acme token_cost=~2.1M-tokens
initial_hypothesis: Preliminary signals point to an accounting skew between the per-route concurrent window and the tenant token bucket: the batch ingestion is causing fast token depletion at the tenant level and the gateway/edge layer may be attributing some preflight or multiplexed subrequests to the streaming route during HTTP/2/GRPC multiplexing. Alternatively, edge shard affinity may be returning stale refill states to a subset of edge nodes (shard-out-of-sync).
investigation_notes: 2026-03-10 03:10 - Liam O'Connor: Pulled rate-limiter logs for tenant acct:acme across us-east. Saw small set of edge nodes (edge-03, edge-05) reporting unexpected token_deltas at pulse time.

2026-03-10 05:20 - SRE (Diego Alvarez): Confirmed batch job issues ~2.1M token cost per pulse; tenant-level refill happened but route-level concurrency window for /v1/stream was exhausted on some shards leading to 429s being served despite global tenant tokens available.

2026-03-11 09:40 - Eng (Priya Rao): Found a race in edge cache invalidation where gRPC stream subrequests are mapped to route id 'chat' but some intermediary preflight/keepalive probes were being accounted as 'default' route on other shards; this caused double-counting into route windows while tenant bucket stayed healthy.
comments: Maya Chen (Support) 2026-03-09T23:12: Customer reports 429 spikes only during their hourly ingest. They've temporarily staggered ingest and saw reduction in 429s.
Liam O'Connor (SRE) 2026-03-10T03:25: Collecting per-edge shard counters. Asking customer for a HAR of their batch job to confirm whether any signed-url preflights are present.
Customer (Acme) 2026-03-10T04:02: Provided HAR + job manifest. Not using signed URLs; batch posts go straight to /v1/embeddings via GraphQL endpoint.

Priya Rao (Eng) 2026-03-11T10:05: Reproduced locally with a tenant-level test harness: multiplexed gRPC + batched HTTP pulses cause route-window exhaustion on coalesced shard; raising route window reduces 429s but does not fully eliminate.
Support (Maya) 2026-03-12T08:42: Proposed mitigations to customer (see resolution).
temporary_workarounds: 1) Stagger batch ingestion pulses across time windows to avoid pulse alignment with chat peak (customer already tested this).
2) Create a separate API key for batch ingestion (segregate tenant-wide accounting across keys).
3) Increase per-route concurrency window for /v1/stream via Console route-level override (short-term mitigation).
root_cause: Race condition and shard-level route attribution during GRPC multiplexing caused some keepalive/preflight subrequests to be attributed to the streaming route on specific edge shards; combined with a large, synchronized batch token pulse this exhausted the per-route concurrency window on those shards and returned 429s even though global tenant tokens were available.
resolution: Eng implemented a two-part fix: 1) Patch to edge proxy to ensure consistent route attribution for multiplexed gRPC subrequests and to ignore internal keepalive probes for accounting; PR merged: github.com/redwood-infer/edge-proxy/pull/1423. 2) Adjusted shard refill sync to propagate tenant token state on warm failover; rollout scheduled to all us-east edges on 2026-03-12 02:00 UTC with gradual canary.
post_resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 02:25 Deployment: canary on edge-01/02 passed smoke tests for 30m with no 429s under test harness.
2026-03-12 04:00 Full rollout: no customer regressions observed; Acme confirmed drop to <0.1% 429s during their scheduled pulse.
Follow-up: Add testing harness for mixed-workload pulses in our e2e rate-limiter test suite (owner: Priya Rao).
related_followups: TASK-2178: Add mixed-load e2e test for multiplexed streams + batch pulses
DOCS-551: Update guidance on segregation of API keys for high-throughput background jobs
closing_notes: Customer confirmed resolution and accepted recommendation to separate long-running batch ingestion onto its own API key for production. Internal follow-ups created for hardened tests and docs. Ticket closed after 48h observation window.
notes_for_billing: No billing discrepancy found; token costs for the batch pulses were correct and charged to Acme. Inform billing to expect no invoice adjustments.
customer_communication: 2026-03-12 05:12 - Maya Chen: Sent final postmortem and recommended short-term segregations.
2026-03-12 06:00 - Acme (Support Lead): Confirmed they will rotate to separate key for batch ingestion and acknowledged root cause.
